summary: Iteration 136 release-candidate check of the iter135 follow-up fixes. All backend tests ran against the isolated real-Mongo DB tejas_isolated_iter134: every Motor handle was rebound (leftover check empty), no lifespan ran, and the DB was dropped after each run (none left). Results: (1) Rerun of the two iter135 suites passed 50/50 with no xfail. That includes test_exam_navigation_history_embargo_and_status_use_db_clock (summary not leaked, still active in DB) plus the replay-25, save/seal race, ledger, pack cache, admission and status tests. (2) The new suite test_iter136_db_clock_release_isolated.py passed 22 of 23 tests. All three files together: 72 passed, 1 failed. (3) The iter105 and iter106 series suites passed 71/71 using a new test-only plugin that overrides the separate DB-clock authority (database_now and clocked_one) to the suite's fixed calendar clock. Without the plugin, 16 tests fail as expected, because the code now reads the Mongo clock. (4) Browser tests ran at exactly 1920x800 and 390x844 against the preview frontend, with /api routed to the iter135 isolated bridge and the session mocked. They passed. (5) The production build (BUILD_PATH=/tmp, then removed) compiled with lint warnings only. NEW FUNCTIONAL FAULT: scheduled private import or chapter-book tests can be started early when the app clock is ahead. content.permitted() still uses the app clock now(); with app +7200 a student started a test whose DB start_at is 1h in the future, and got 200 with the question text. Verdict: not release-ready until that gate uses the DB clock, unless the operator accepts the NTP-skew risk. No 500k, capacity or security-complete claim is made.

With the app clock +7200 and DB start_at = real+3600, a student's start returned 200 with the full question text before the Mongo release time. critical_code_review_comments: Satellite embargo gates (reviews, ai_solutions, mock_solutions, cohorts, learning_progress, question_reports, jobs.download, exam_navigation, chapter_books, my_tests, live_series, competitions) now use _database_now, EPOCH_NOW or database_now, and were verified via the API at +/-7200.
jobs.download now scopes the attempt lookup by user_id and returns 404 when the attempt is missing. This is good.
attempts.py still has a.get('_database_now', now()) fallbacks. They are harmless now, because owned and db.get always clock, but they hide future regressions; prefer a['_database_now'].
http_limits special-cases the 'jobs.cron' key for 400. That works, but a per-contract status attribute would be cleaner.
